prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 topological insulator, and for its first experimental realisation in HgTe quantum wells

statement.case_for: The Z2 topological insulator changed how band structure is classified: a time-reversal-invariant insulator can carry protected edge or surface states with no broken symmetry behind them. Kane and Mele supplied the concept and the invariant, and Molenkamp's group showed the helical edge conduction in HgTe/CdTe wells with quantized conductance. Interpretation has been stable for almost two decades, through transport, ARPES on Bi-based three-dimensional materials and a large body of first-principles calculation. That ab initio work has predicted and screened candidate materials, which I can judge from my own field. It is a clean theory-plus-experiment story with a short, well-defined chain of prediction and observation.
statement.case_against: The 2016 prize covered topological phase transitions and topological phases of matter, so a sceptic can call this a continuation. The supplied credit also leaves out Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, whose HgTe prediction was what made the experiment possible, and Zhang is deceased. The three-person limit forces an uncomfortable attribution to Molenkamp alone on the experimental side, and the Fu-Kane-Mele and Moore-Balents work on three-dimensional insulators is a separate allocation. Opening support is thin: only I ranked it first, and four colleagues placed it sixth or lower. I must weigh that and not simply defend my own list.

responses.point: Ranked magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene (B022) first as a nature-led discovery, preceded by a sharp prediction, with a Bistritzer-MacDonald plus Jarillo-Herrero theory-plus-experiment trio.
responses.response: I agree that B022 is the strongest candidate on breadth of impact and rate of replication, and I ranked it third. My hesitation is maturity. The pairing mechanism and the origin of the correlated phases are unsettled, and twist-angle disorder limits reproducibility from sample to sample. A prize awarded now to the discovery and prediction is defensible, but I would still prefer to wait for a more settled interpretation. Your point about Yuan Cao being outside the credited names is real: it makes the experimental side harder to defend than the Kane-Mele-Molenkamp chain. I keep B022 as my first alternative rather than my preferred configuration.

responses.point: Ranked optical lattice clocks (B036) first: the magic-wavelength concept of Katori with Ye's record accuracy, a clean two-person credit, confirmed independently across Sr, Yb and Hg, and timely whether or not the second is redefined.
responses.response: You make the cleanest attribution case of any candidate, and I moved B036 from my opening eighth place to my second alternative. Clock performance is far from my field, so I defer to you on the physics. My remaining reservation is novelty. Combs were recognised in 2005 and ion control in 2012, and the committee would have to judge that lattice clocks are a distinct discovery and not an engineering refinement of that lineage. If you and Stefan Kroll can show that the magic-wavelength idea is the decisive conceptual step, I would take B036 as a serious configuration.

responses.point: Placed B054 seventh because its depth is real but it extends the topological classification already honoured in 2016, and the HgTe prediction credit is missing from the supplied names.
responses.response: The overlap with 2016 is the strongest objection to my first choice, and I do not dismiss it. I read the 2016 citation as being about topological invariants in phase transitions and in the quantum Hall and Haldane-type setting, with time-reversal symmetry not broken. Kane and Mele supplied a different step: a symmetry-protected phase with no magnetic field, and the first realisation of it. On credit I agree it is imperfect. Molenkamp is the experimental anchor, but the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang gap cannot be repaired within three names.

responses.point: Ranked circuit QED (B044) first as the basis of present superconducting processors, while openly noting close professional familiarity and a likely overlap with the 2025 prize.
responses.response: Thank you for stating the familiarity openly. I take the overlap risk seriously. I chaired the committee for the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits, and a second superconducting-circuit award within a year would be hard to explain, even though circuit QED is a distinct achievement. Credit also remains open, since Wallraff is not among the supplied names. For those reasons I do not place B044 in my configuration or alternatives.

uncertainties: Whether the 2016 prize leaves enough room for a distinct topological-insulator award is a judgement call on which colleagues will plausibly split.
Whether the credited three names can be defended without Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, given Zhang's death.
Whether the committee should move first to magic-angle graphene (B022) despite the unresolved pairing mechanism, because it has the broadest opening support.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile. I work in electronic-structure theory and have published on two-dimensional materials, but the profile documents no personal or institutional tie to Kane, Mele, Molenkamp or the other shortlisted candidates. I note that I chaired the 2025 cycle, which bears on the overlap argument for B044 but is not a personal conflict.
